title: Zeta-regularization and natural boundaries: Sums and products of integers and primes
summary: arXiv:2606.24536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Euler regularized the divergent product of all positive integers and found beautiful formulas for regularized sums of integer powers of positive integers. These derivations essentially relied on what is now called the zeta-regularization technique, although analytical continuation had not yet been invented. This classic method is however not applicable to the product of all primes, as the prime zeta function has a natural boundary along the imaginary axis. Mu\~noz Garc\'ia and P\'erez-Marco overcame this obstacle and evaluated the product of all primes to $4\pi^2$ by finding an appropriately regularized value of the derivative of the prime zeta function at the origin, lying on the natural boundary. Their approach heavily relies on the M\"obius function and could therefore be called a M\"obius regularization. We extend this approach in two novel directions. First, we show how to make sense of the sum of all primes. This regularization requires going a finite distance beyond the natural boundary. title: Yau's pinching problem and vanishing of Betti numbers
summary: arXiv:2611.27950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a closed connected Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq4$, satisfying $\sec>\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$ at every point has vanishing real cohomology in degrees $1,..., n-1$. It is consequently a rational homology sphere if $n$ is odd or the manifold is orientable. Complex projective space shows that the coefficient is optimal and that the strict inequality is necessary in every even dimension. The required estimate for the Weitzenb\"ock curvature term is established by integrating restricted Ricci operators over orthonormal frames and combining complementary degrees using Hodge duality. This also allows us to replace sectional curvature pinching by intermediate Ricci curvature bounds. For a nonflat metric, the weak Yau inequality, $\sec\geq\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$, gives the same cohomology vanishing unless the manifold is isometric, up to scaling, to a quotient of complex projective space with its Fubini-Study metric. title: Yau's first eigenvalue conjecture for embedded minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature
summary: arXiv:2611.26893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M^n$ be a smooth closed connected embedded minimal hypersurface of the unit sphere. Suppose that $M$ has constant scalar curvature. We prove that its first positive Laplace eigenvalue is $n$ and that the ambient coordinate functions span its first eigenspace. To prove both assertions, we consider an eigenfunction $f$ with eigenvalue $0<\lambda\le n$ orthogonal to every coordinate function. We use $f$ as the density of a single-layer potential on the sphere. The geometry of $M$ gives a lower bound for the Dirichlet energy of this potential. The spherical heat kernel gives a smaller upper bound for the same energy. This contradiction rules out every such nonzero $f$.
